title: GRPO Beyond English: A Large-Scale Study of GRPO in Non-English and Multilingual Settings
gist: A large-scale empirical study of GRPO-based Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) applied to non-English and multilingual reasoning, spanning many base models, training languages, and reasoning-language rewards. It finds that native-language reasoning training leaves only a small gap to English training and transfers across languages, but can also cause severe out-of-domain regressions, so broad evaluation is required.

insights.claim: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), often optimized with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), has become a central recipe for improving reasoning in pretrained language models, but existing studies remain heavily English-centric.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Frames the whitespace this study fills: reasoning-RL evidence has been almost entirely English so far.
insights.quote: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), often optimized with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), has become a central recipe for improving the reasoning capabilities of pretrained language models but current studies remain heavily English-centric.

insights.claim: Training a model to reason in its native language often leaves only a small performance gap relative to training for English reasoning.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Suggests teams can train reasoning in the target language without a large penalty versus defaulting to English.
insights.quote: We find that training to reason in the native language often leaves only a small gap to training for English reasoning.
insights.locator: We find that training to reason in the native language

insights.claim: The study observes strong crosslingual transfer, where GRPO training in one language often improves reasoning performance in many other languages.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Crosslingual transfer means one language's RL run can lift a whole multilingual model, lowering per-language training cost.
insights.quote: We further observe strong crosslingual transfer: training in one language often improves performance in many others.
insights.locator: We further observe strong crosslingual transfer

insights.claim: The authors find that GRPO trends are highly model- and language-dependent, and that training in a particular language can induce severe regressions on out-of-domain capabilities in other languages.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The upside of transfer comes with a downside risk: gains in one language can quietly break others, so per-language evaluation is not optional.
insights.quote: In some cases, training in a particular language induces severe regressions on out-of-domain capabilities in other languages.
insights.locator: However, specific trends are highly model- and language-dependent

insights.claim: The analysis concludes that RLVR beyond English can deliver broad crosslingual gains but also requires broad evaluation to detect language-specific regressions.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Actionable takeaway for practitioners: pair multilingual RL training with wide multilingual eval to catch hidden regressions.
